title: Qafzeh and Skhul caves, Israel: early modern human burials
summary: Qafzeh Cave, on a hillside near Nazareth, and Skhul Cave on Mount Carmel, both in Israel, hold clusters of Paleolithic burials. Thermoluminescence and electron spin resonance readings date the two clusters to about 120,000–90,000 years ago, which made them the oldest modern human fossils found outside Africa until the Misliya find.

uncertainty.note: Years before present in the sources are written here as negative calendar years without subtracting 1950; the sources give rounded ages. Qafzeh thermoluminescence on burnt flint gave a mean of 92,000 ± 5,000 (Valladas et al. 1988) and ESR on enamel about 115 ka (Schwarcz et al. 1988), as reported in PALEO.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the pin: the two caves are about 40 km apart, so the main point sits at Qafzeh and Skhul is a second region. Wikidata labels Qafzeh's country differently from the PALEO article, which places it in Galilee, Israel; the article was followed. The dates are those quoted in the sources, not recomputed.
